base_member_text: [L1-L3] (LOW/provenance/stale-instruction) The edit instruction refers to `variable.f90` instead of the actual `variables.def` source.
audit_member_text: [L1-L3] (LOW/generation-contract/documentation) The header names variable.f90 as the editable source although the template consumes generated variable metadata.

base_member_text: [L17-L21,L33,L38] (MED/generation/type-map) The type map expects the key `character`, while `generate.py` maps Fortran character declarations to `char`, and it also omits other generator-supported mapped types, so a newly supported variable type can fail generation with a key error.
audit_member_text: [L17-L21,L33,L38] (LOW/schema/extensibility) The type-to-code mapping is a closed three-entry dictionary with direct lookup, so any definition using an otherwise valid new type causes generation to fail with no validation-oriented diagnostic.

adversarial.rationale: The char/character mismatch and direct KeyError on additional mapped types are real latent extension problems, but all 327 current variables are double or int. mnemonic.F90:10-33 also provides only real/integer pointer members, so a type merely accepted by generate.py is not already supported by the introspection contract; this requires a coordinated type-system extension, not just correction of one dictionary key.

base_member_text: [L37-L46] (LOW/state/reuse) Rank-specific dimensions are written only for positive rank and unused dimension slots are never cleared, leaving stale dimension text possible when an introspection object is reused unless every consumer strictly honors `t%rank`.

audit_member_text: [L39-L43] (MED/code-generation/escaping) Definition strings are interpolated directly inside single-quoted Fortran literals without escaping embedded apostrophes, making a legitimate metadata value capable of producing malformed generated source.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: L39-L43 embed metadata directly in single-quoted Fortran literals, with no escaping helper or filter in the enclosing template. generate.py also preserves apostrophes in descriptions and JSON strings without sanitization, so a value such as beach's elevation produces an undoubled apostrophe and a malformed Fortran literal.

adversarial.rationale: The actual variable regex preserves an apostrophe in a description such as water's depth, and indextos.mako:43 then inserts it inside a single-quoted Fortran literal without doubling it. No parser sanitization or Mako lookup filter escapes Fortran literals; existing descriptions contain no apostrophes, but a legitimate new description directly triggers malformed output.
